## Ideal-moist closure and the kintera thermodynamics (`ideal-moist`) {#sec-ch02-ideal-moist}

### Summary

The ideal-moist closure describes dry air plus vapours and condensates, each with a constant heat capacity and
a reference energy. Vapours are ideal gases; condensates carry mass and heat but no pressure. The closure turns
the stored energy into pressure through two mixture factors, gives the mixture's ratio of specific heats, and
splits the energy and enthalpy fluxes by species. It is the closure of every moist deck that a CUDA graph may
capture, and the only one that supports anomaly storage (@sec-ch02-laws).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Pressure from the stored energy, @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-energy, with the factors of @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-factors.

**Data.** Reads $\rho_{\mathrm d}$[^rg-fdddc3879e36], $\rho_n$[^rg-49a92914133c], $\mathbf m$, $E$; writes $p$, $y_n$[^rg-af1921a9322a], $T$, $\gamma$. Species constants from kintera.

**Placement.** Every `"U->W"` and `"W->U"`; `"U'->W"` with anomaly storage; `"W->A"` for the Riemann solver.

**Activation.** `dynamics/equation-of-state/type: ideal-moist`, with a `species`[^rg-e2c86a33eac7] list for kintera.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact inverse in exact arithmetic; constant heat capacities only.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch02-ideal-moist-tests: `test_eos.release`, `test_eos_temp2inteng_python`, `test_eos_species_sum_layout_python`.
:::

Local symbols: $\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}$ the thermal energy density $\rho e$ minus the reference energies [J m$^{-3}$];
$\mathcal G=\sum\rho_nR_n$ over dry air and vapours, the gas term [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\mathcal C_v=\sum\rho_nc_{v,n}$
over dry air and all species, the heat capacity per volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]. These three appear only in the
anomaly perturbation split.

### Derivation

#### The mixture factors

Dry air and each species $n$ have constant $c_{v,n}$[^rg-8a1c96767aef], and gases have $R_n=\mathcal R/\mu_n$. Three steps:

1. *Pressure from the gases.* Dalton's law sums the partial pressures of dry air and the vapours,
   $p=\bigl(\rho_{\mathrm d}R_{\mathrm d}+\sum_{n\in\mathcal V}\rho_nR_n\bigr)T$. Condensates add nothing.
2. *Normalize by the dry gas.* Divide by $\rho R_{\mathrm d}T$: dry air contributes $1-\sum_ny_n$, a vapour
   $y_n\mu_{\mathrm d}/\mu_n$, a condensate nothing. Collecting gives $p=\rho R_{\mathrm d}f_\varepsilon T$.
3. *Heat capacity from all species.* $\rho c_v=\rho_{\mathrm d}c_{v,\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nc_{v,n}$; dividing by
   $\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}$ gives $c_v=c_{v,\mathrm d}f_\sigma$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_\varepsilon&=1+\sum_{n\in\mathcal V}y_n(\mu_{\mathrm d}/\mu_n-1)-\sum_{n\in\mathcal C}y_n,\\
f_\sigma&=1+\sum_n y_n(c_{v,n}/c_{v,\mathrm d}-1).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-factors}

@eq-ch02-ideal-moist-factors is implemented by `IdealMoistImpl::f_eps`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::f_eps >}}) and `IdealMoistImpl::f_sig`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::f_sig >}}), from the coefficients $\mu_{\mathrm d}/\mu_n-1$ and
$c_{v,n}/c_{v,\mathrm d}-1$ that `IdealMoistImpl::reset` ({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::reset >}})
builds once from the kintera species table. Check `[V4]` confirms that the two factors equal
$(\rho_{\mathrm d}R_{\mathrm d}+\sum_{\mathcal V}\rho_nR_n)/(\rho R_{\mathrm d})$ and $\rho c_v/(\rho c_{v,\mathrm d})$.

#### Energy, pressure and temperature

Each species carries a reference energy $u^\star_n=u^{\mathrm{ref}}_n\mathcal R/\mu_n$ [J kg$^{-1}$], and dry air
$u^\star_{\mathrm d}$. The specific internal energy of the mixture is the mass-weighted sum of
$u^\star_n+c_{v,n}T$. Three more steps:

4. *Energy.* $\rho e=\rho_{\mathrm d}u^\star_{\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nu^\star_n+\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}f_\sigma T$.
5. *Eliminate $T$.* Solve $p=\rho R_{\mathrm d}f_\varepsilon T$ for $T$, substitute into step 4, and use
   $R_{\mathrm d}=(\gamma_{\mathrm d}-1)c_{v,\mathrm d}$.
6. *Collect.*

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho e&=\rho_{\mathrm d}u_{\mathrm d}^\star+\sum_n\rho_nu_n^\star
+\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}f_\sigma T,\\
p&=\rho R_{\mathrm d}f_\varepsilon T,\\
p&=\frac{(\gamma_{\mathrm d}-1)f_\varepsilon}{f_\sigma}
\left(\rho e-\rho_{\mathrm d}u_{\mathrm d}^\star-\sum_n\rho_nu_n^\star\right).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-energy}

@eq-ch02-ideal-moist-energy is implemented by `IdealMoistImpl::_cons2prim`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_cons2prim >}}) for the last row, by
`IdealMoistImpl::_prim2intEng` ({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_prim2intEng >}}) for its
inverse, and by `IdealMoistImpl::_prim2temp` ({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_prim2temp >}})
for $T=p/(\rho R_{\mathrm d}f_\varepsilon)$. `gammad` is the dry ratio of specific heats of the EOS block, and
`weight` its dry molar mass; neither is used as given: `MoistEOSImpl::sync_dry_options_`
({{< code src/eos/moist_base.cpp MoistEOSImpl::sync_dry_options_ >}}) overwrites `gammad` with
$1+1/c^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathrm d}$ and `weight` with the dry species' molar mass when the closure is built. Here
$\gamma_{\mathrm d}=(c^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathrm d}+1)/c^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathrm d}$ with
$c^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathrm d}=c_{v,\mathrm d}/R_{\mathrm d}$, from `gammad_`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.hpp IdealMoistImpl::gammad_ >}}), which is $1+R_{\mathrm d}/c_{v,\mathrm d}$
(`[V4]`).

The two directions use the reference energies in two forms. `_prim2intEng` writes them with the primitive
fractions, $\rho(1-\sum_ny_n)u^\star_{\mathrm d}+\rho\sum_ny_nu^\star_n$; `_cons2prim` subtracts them with the
conserved rows, $\rho_{\mathrm d}u^\star_{\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nu^\star_n$. By @eq-ch02-laws-state these are the
same number in exact arithmetic, so the round trip returns $p$ exactly (`[V5]`).

#### The energy at a given temperature, and the offset

The key `"UT->I"` is `IdealMoistImpl::_temp2intEng`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_temp2intEng >}}), which uses only conserved rows:

$$
\rho e(T)=\rho_{\mathrm d}u^\star_{\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nu^\star_n
+\Bigl(\rho_{\mathrm d}c_{v,\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nc_{v,n}\Bigr)T .
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-offset}

@eq-ch02-ideal-moist-offset is implemented by `IdealMoistImpl::_temp2intEng`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_temp2intEng >}}). Its first two terms are the energy offset,
`IdealMoistImpl::internal_energy_offset`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::internal_energy_offset >}}). Two properties follow:

- At the state's own temperature, @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-offset equals the first row of
  @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-energy, because $\rho_{\mathrm d}c_{v,\mathrm d}+\sum_n\rho_nc_{v,n}=\rho c_{v,\mathrm d}f_\sigma$
  (`[V5]`). The temperature floor of @sec-ch08 relies on it.
- $\rho e(T)$ is affine in $T$ with the offset as its intercept: $u^\star_n$ is added, never scaled by $T$
  (`[V5]`). `test_eos_temp2inteng_python` measures both properties.

#### The mixture heat ratio and the enthalpy split

At fixed composition, $c_p-c_v=R_{\mathrm d}f_\varepsilon$. Dividing by $c_v=c_{v,\mathrm d}f_\sigma$:

$$
\gamma=1+(\gamma_{\mathrm d}-1)f_\varepsilon/f_\sigma .
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-gamma}

@eq-ch02-ideal-moist-gamma is the `"W->A"` branch of `IdealMoistImpl::compute`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::compute >}}). It equals $c_p/c_v$ of the mixture with
condensates counted in $c_v$[^rg-107866fa20ba] and not in the gas term (`[V5]`). It is the frozen ratio: phase change during a sound
wave is not included.

The closure also splits the energy flux $(E+p)\mathbf v$ by species.
`IdealMoistImpl::species_enthalpy`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::species_enthalpy >}}) gives, per unit mass of species $n$,

$$
\hat h_n+\tfrac12 g_{ab}v_av_b=u^\star_n+\bigl(c_{v,n}+R_n\bigr)T+\tfrac12 g_{ab}v_av_b,
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-enthalpy}

with $R_n=0$ for a condensate. @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-enthalpy is implemented by
`IdealMoistImpl::species_enthalpy` ({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::species_enthalpy >}}). With
the dry analogue $u^\star_{\mathrm d}+(c_{v,\mathrm d}+R_{\mathrm d})T$ plus the
kinetic energy, the mass-weighted sum over dry air and all species is $(E+p)/\rho$ (`[V6]`). The code returns
the species rows only; the dry share is the remainder.

#### The anomaly perturbation split

With anomaly storage the closure also has to give the pressure of a state that differs slightly from its
reference without losing the small difference to rounding. `IdealMoistImpl::perturbations`
({{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::perturbations >}}) writes the pressure as
$p=\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}\mathcal G/\mathcal C_v$, where step 2 and step 4 give
$\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}=\mathcal C_vT$ and $p=\mathcal GT$ (`[V9]`). With reference values
$\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}$ and differences
$\delta\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}$, $\delta\mathcal G$, $\delta\mathcal C_v$ formed from the stored anomaly rows, the
pressure difference is

$$
\delta p=\frac{\delta\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}\,(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\mathcal G)
+\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}_{\mathrm{ref}}\,\delta\mathcal G-p_{\mathrm{ref}}\,\delta\mathcal C_v}
{\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\mathcal C_v},
$$ {#eq-ch02-ideal-moist-perturbation}

with $p_{\mathrm{ref}}=\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}_{\mathrm{ref}}\mathcal G_{\mathrm{ref}}/\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}$.
@eq-ch02-ideal-moist-perturbation is kintera's `eval_const_cv_pressure_delta`
([`kintera eval_uhs.hpp:44-52`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0429d795f79a0665afeca565e5a05c87ab4ba1e2/src/thermo/eval_uhs.hpp#L44-L52)),
called by `perturbations`. It is the exact difference
$(\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}_{\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\Theta^{\mathrm{th}})(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\mathcal G)
/(\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\mathcal C_v)-p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, rearranged so that no large term is
subtracted from another (`[V9]`). The kinetic energy in $\delta\Theta^{\mathrm{th}}$ is formed with the raised
momenta of @eq-ch02-laws-metric.

Exact and truncated: @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-factors to @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-perturbation are exact in exact
arithmetic for constant heat capacities. Nothing is iterated: with constant $c_{v,n}$ the energy is linear in
$T$ and the inversion is closed form.

### Numerical method

The conversion is pointwise, as for the ideal gas (@sec-ch02-ideal-gas). The species sums
$\sum_ny_nc_n$ are accumulated one species at a time by `species_dot`
({{< code src/eos/species_sum.hpp species_dot >}}), not by a matrix product: a product over the species axis of
a block's strided layout rounds by memory position, so two identical columns could differ by one unit in the
last place. `test_eos_species_sum_layout_python` checks that identical $x_2$ columns give bitwise identical
results. @fig-ch02-ideal-moist-flow shows the order of the conversion.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch02-ideal-moist-flow
#| fig-cap: "Mass fractions set the mixture factors used to convert thermal energy into gas pressure."
#| fig-alt: "Mass fractions set the mixture factors used to convert thermal energy into gas pressure."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch02.figures.fig_ideal_moist_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** The species come from the kintera part of the deck:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `name`[^rg-e6bf2057e7b8], `composition`[^rg-e540c1be9eba], `N`[^rg-b5dfd97dcd83], `cv_R`[^rg-69a0a493850f].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-moist}
species:
  - {name: dry, composition: {N: 2}, cv_R: 2.5}
```

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *Perturbations without a reference.* `perturbations` refuses a block with no anomaly reference or with no
   species reference ("this legacy restart only supports anomaly storage").
2. *Perturbations with variable heat capacities.* It refuses a kintera table with NASA-9 or H2 heat capacities:
   @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-perturbation assumes constant $c_{v,n}$.
3. *A non-positive heat capacity.* `perturbations` checks that $\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}$ and
   $\mathcal C_{v,\mathrm{ref}}+\delta\mathcal C_v$ are finite and positive. In a captured stage the check is
   deferred: a failure latches the EfStatus heat-capacity slot and the step is rejected (@sec-ch08).

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| keys | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::compute >}} | `compute` | `ideal-moist` |
| mixture factors | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::f_eps >}} | `f_eps`, `f_sig` | |
| pressure from energy | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_cons2prim >}} | `_cons2prim` | |
| energy from pressure | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_prim2intEng >}} | `_prim2intEng` | |
| energy at a temperature | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::_temp2intEng >}} | `_temp2intEng` | |
| anomaly split | {{< code src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp IdealMoistImpl::perturbations >}} | `perturbations` | `anomaly` |

The constants are built in `IdealMoistImpl::reset`: `inv_mu_ratio_m1` holds $\mu_{\mathrm d}/\mu_n-1$,
`cv_ratio_m1` holds $c_{v,n}/c_{v,\mathrm d}-1$, and the buffer `u0` holds $u^\star$ for dry air and then each
species, as `uref_R` times $\mathcal R/\mu_n$.

#### The H2–He decks

Six decks under `examples/` model a giant-planet atmosphere with the same thermodynamic choices. The H$_2$–He
background is **one lumped species named `dry`** with the elemental composition `{H: 1.5, He: 0.15}` and the
constant `cv_R: 2.5`. There is no ortho/para treatment: `use-h2-cp` is off, and it would not apply anyway, because it
acts only on a species named exactly `H2` (@sec-ch02-moist-mixture). The condensables are extra species with their
own constant `cv_R` and an energy offset `u0_R`[^rg-fa067cae2716]. The numbers C1–C14 below are independent arithmetic and a port of
the rotor formula, not a kintera run.[^h2he-run]

| $T$-dependent $c_p$ | `reference-state: use-nasa9-cp`, `use-h2-cp`, `h2-cp-mode` | off, off, `equilibrium` (@sec-ch02-moist-mixture) |

: Where the thermodynamic choices are configured. {#tbl-ch02-h2he-choices}

No deck or test at the pin sets `use-h2-cp` or `use-nasa9-cp` (a search of `examples/` and `tests/` at the pin).
**Hypothesis about composition, not author intent.** If `{H: 1.5, He: 0.15}` were meant as 0.75 H$_2$ plus 0.15 He
molecules, the molecular mixture would have mean molar mass 2.347 g/mol and He mole fraction 1/6 (C10). No source
establishes that interpretation, and the reason for `cv_R: 2.5` is also unsourced.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| {{< code tests/test_eos_temp2inteng.py main >}} (`test_eos_temp2inteng_python`) | `"UT->I"` equals `"W->I"` at 50, 100, 200 and 400 K; affine in $T$; intercept is the offset | rel. $10^{-12}$, $10^{-12}$, $10^{-10}$ | `--rtol` default; literals in the test |
| {{< code tests/test_eos.cpp DeviceTest.ideal_moist_internal_energy_offset >}} (`test_eos.release`) | the offset of @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-offset | rtol $10^{-6}$, atol $10^{-6}$ | `torch::allclose` in the test |
| {{< code tests/test_eos.cpp DeviceTest.ideal_moist_pressure_perturbations_include_species_and_ke >}} (`test_eos.release`) | $\delta p$ and $\delta\rho$ against the total-state difference | rtol $2\times10^{-6}$; atol $10^{-7}$, $10^{-12}$ | `torch::allclose` in the test |
| {{< code tests/test_eos_species_sum_layout.py main >}} (`test_eos_species_sum_layout_python`) | identical $x_2$ columns give identical `"W->A"`, `"W->T"`, `"W->I"`, `"W->U"`, `"U->W"` | bitwise | `x != x[..., :1, :]` count is 0 |

: Tests of the ideal-moist closure. {#tbl-ch02-ideal-moist-tests}

Two more ctests touch the closure. `DeviceTest.ideal_moist_pressure_perturbations_preserve_small_heating` checks
$\delta p$ with rtol $2\times10^{-6}$, atol $10^{-10}$, and the reference pressure with rtol $10^{-14}$, atol
$10^{-8}$; `DeviceTest.ideal_moist_pressure_perturbations_without_condensables` uses rtol $2\times10^{-7}$, atol
$10^{-10}$. `test_sk1_failure_counter_python` checks that the kintera failure counter rows 1 and 2 reach the
register's monitor and are left untouched by the redo decision (one `torch.equal`); the counter belongs to
@sec-ch08.

`DeviceTest` runs on CPU and CUDA, FP32 and FP64. The Python tests run on CPU; `test_sk1_failure_counter` and
`test_anomaly_storage` are also registered with `--device cuda`. At the pin every test of the table passes.[^ideal-moist-run]
In `test_eos_temp2inteng_python` the round-trip error at the four temperatures, the curvature of $\rho e(T)$ and
the error of its intercept are all below $10^{-14}$ relative, against thresholds of $10^{-12}$, $10^{-12}$ and
$10^{-10}$; these are round-off, so the text quotes them against the threshold, not to digits.

[^ideal-moist-run]: [sha: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062; deck: the tests' own inputs
    (`tests/test_eos.yaml`, `tests/test_anomaly_storage.yaml`, `tests/test_eos_temp2inteng.yaml` and the decks the other
    tests build); run: `ctest -j1 -V -R <name>` for the eight ctests `test_eos.release`, `test_aneos_gamma.release`,
    `test_anomaly_storage_python`, `test_anomaly_storage_cuda_python`, `test_eos_temp2inteng_python`,
    `test_eos_species_sum_layout_python`, `test_sk1_failure_counter_python` and `test_sk1_failure_counter_cuda_python`,
    run together with one anchored `-R` pattern, in the `tests` directory of a README CUDA Release build at the pin; CPU
    and one CUDA GPU, FP32 and FP64 as each test sets them, 1 rank; Python 3.11.13, torch 2.10.0+cu128, numpy 2.4.6,
    kintera 2.6.13, pyharp 2.8.2]. 8 of 8 ctests passed; `test_eos.release` ran 43 gtest cases, 18 of them on CUDA.

### Limits

1. **Constant heat capacities.** $c_{v,n}$ are the constants of the kintera table; `perturbations` refuses
   NASA-9 and H2 heat capacities, and the main conversion reads only the constants. A temperature-dependent
   heat capacity needs an iterative inversion, which the code does not have.
2. **Frozen sound speed.** @eq-ch02-ideal-moist-gamma ignores phase change within a wave period.
3. **Untested combinations.** Switch-combination coverage is in @sec-ch12-matrix.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-fdddc3879e36]: $\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$ — dry-air density [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-49a92914133c]: $\rho_n$ — partial density of species $n$, $\rho y_n$ [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-af1921a9322a]: $y_n$ — mass fraction of species $n$ **per unit total mass**, $\rho_n = \rho y_n$, dimensionless [-]; this is snapy's composition variable and the only one the state vector carries

[^rg-e2c86a33eac7]: species — species definitions or selection in the enclosing thermodynamic block

[^rg-8a1c96767aef]: $c_{v,n}, c_{p,n}$ — specific heats of species $n$ at constant volume and pressure, **per unit mass of that species** [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $c_{v,n} = c^{\mathrm{ref}}_n R_n$ with $c^{\mathrm{ref}}_n$ the dimensionless table value. $n=\mathrm{d}$ is dry air: $c_{v,\mathrm{d}}, c_{p,\mathrm{d}}$

[^rg-107866fa20ba]: $c_v, c_p$ — mixture specific heats **per unit total mass**, $c_v = \sum_n y_n c_{v,n}$ over dry air and every species [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; a chapter that needs the per-dry-mass form writes it out and says so

[^rg-e6bf2057e7b8]: name — name identifying the enclosing component

[^rg-e540c1be9eba]: composition — elemental composition of a species

[^rg-b5dfd97dcd83]: N — nitrogen count in the composition mapping

[^rg-69a0a493850f]: cv_R — reference heat capacity divided by the species gas constant

[^rg-fa067cae2716]: u0_R — reference internal energy in the species gas-constant normalisation

[^rg-8291c2d31ed0]: $R_n = \mathcal R/\mu_n$ — specific gas constant of species $n$ [J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; defined for gases only, a condensate has no $R_n$ and contributes no pressure; `Ri` in the code; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L40-L43)

[^rg-d2638fa4bcad]: Tref — thermodynamic reference temperature

[^rg-7058b44e3174]: Pref — thermodynamic reference pressure

[^rg-e37071e794ae]: grav1 — gravity component along the first coordinate

[^rg-e94ee68cfd5d]: $\mu_n$ — molar mass of species $n$ [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $\mu_{\mathrm{d}}$ for dry air. Never bare $\mu$, which is dynamic viscosity (§8); the code stores the inverse
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
